entry.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
entry.summary: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.

entry.title: Internalizing Investment Mandates: A Neurosymbolic RL Approach to Portfolio Allocation
entry.summary: Institutional portfolios operate under investment policy statements that specify asset allocation constraints, often conditioned on market regime information. Deep reinforcement learning has been shown to optimize financial performance but typically does not enforce rule compliance, making it unsuitable for real-world deployment. Existing neurosymbolic methods such as Probabilistic Logic Policy Gradient (PLPG) offer constraint-satisfying reinforcement learning (RL) via differentiable symbolic supervision but assume a finite, discrete action space. We present a PLPG-inspired continuous allocation method that estimates the probability that the policy's own executed action satisfies the investment mandate, using reparameterized Monte Carlo sampling, and adds it to the training objective. No post-hoc enforcement mechanism intercepts actions at inference time and compliance is learned by the agent. Audited directly on deterministic mean actions with no correction, the policy reduces violations of a six-rule regime-conditional mandate from 96-98% for unconstrained RL and 33.4% for a reward-penalty baseline to 4.8%, showing that a continuous-action neurosymbolic policy can substantially internalize a symbolic mandate.

entry.title: A Dark-Sector Mass Flip-Flop Mechanism for the ANITA-IV Events
entry.summary: ANITA-IV has observed four upward-going air-shower candidates just below the horizon, consistent with ultra-high-energy $ν_τ$, yet IceCube, despite its much larger exposure, has detected no neutrino events at such energies. We propose a dark-sector mass flip-flop mechanism that reconciles these observations. We consider an all-sky, monoenergetic flux of ultra-high-energy $N_1$, that is lighter than its partner $N_2$ and stable in vacuum. In our scenario, an ultralight scalar mediating interactions with Earth matter inverts the mass ordering of $N_1$ and $N_2$, allowing an incident $N_1$ to decay into $N_2$ deep underground. The resulting $N_2$ propagates unimpeded through matter and exits the Earth, where the decay $N_2 \to N_1 Z'$ becomes kinematically allowed in the atmosphere, initiating an extensive air shower. At IceCube depths, neither $N_1\to N_2 Z'$ nor $N_2\to N_1 Z'$ is kinematically allowed, which explains the absence of analogous events at IceCube. Normalizing the $N_1$ flux to the four ANITA-IV events, we also predict three events during PUEO's first flight.

entry.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE Agents Leverage Unlabeled Data?
entry.summary: Applying machine learning systems to new domains introduces bottlenecks in both labeled data acquisition and manual pipeline engineering. While recent MLE agents show promise in automating pipeline design, they have been studied almost exclusively in fully supervised settings, leaving them untested in realistic regimes where labeled data is scarce but unlabeled data is abundant. In this work, we introduce Agentic Semi-Supervised Learning (AgentSSL), framing SSL as a program search problem and studying how agents navigate this space under limited supervision. We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%. However, our results identify program selection as a critical bottleneck in AgentSSL, where performance drops by as much as 47% when selecting based on the agent's feedback metric. To systematically study this bottleneck, we introduce ProgramSelectBench, a large-scale benchmark with a combined total of 16,977 agent-generated and human-engineered SSL programs, and evaluate both unsupervised and active program selection methods. We further evaluate AgentSSL on real-world ecology detection tasks, highlighting the opportunities and challenges of transferring agent-discovered strategies beyond controlled benchmarks.

entry.title: The Tournament Equilibrium Set Is PSPACE-Complete, Even under Hereditary Uniqueness
entry.summary: The tournament equilibrium set (TEQ), proposed by Schwartz in 1990, is a classical voting rule based on pairwise majority comparisons. Its definition is recursive: an alternative is judged by the alternatives that beat it, called its dominators, and by which of those dominators TEQ itself selects. Deciding whether a given alternative belongs to TEQ was known to be NP-hard and to lie in PSPACE. We close this gap by proving that the problem is PSPACE-complete. To our knowledge, this is the first PSPACE-completeness result for membership in a tournament solution. The hardness persists even when every nonempty subtournament has a unique minimal retentive set, the property conjectured by Schwartz to hold for all tournaments. Moreover, every such subtournament in our hard instances contains an alternative with at most three dominators. We prove that a single alternative with at most four dominators suffices both to guarantee uniqueness and to find a TEQ winner in $O(N^2)$ time. Thus, on our hard instances, finding one winner is efficient even though recognizing a specified winner is PSPACE-complete. We also study how the complexity changes with the dominator bound. If every nonempty subtournament has an alternative with at most one dominator, the entire TEQ can be computed in quadratic time; allowing two dominators makes membership NP-hard. Under the same condition with four dominators, all $t$ winners can be computed in $O(2^t N^2)$ time, where $N$ is the number of alternatives.

entry.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
entry.summary: The JWST Rocky Worlds Director's Discretionary Time (RWDDT) program uses secondary eclipse observations to determine the conditions under which rocky exoplanets around M dwarfs retain their atmospheres. We present RWDDT MIRI/F1500W observations of LTT 1445 A b and c, the transiting rocky siblings in the nearest such system (6.9 pc), comprising two eclipses of each planet across three visits. We perform three independent reductions and a joint fit that includes all existing JWST data and 220 radial velocities, improving the precision on the planetary radii, masses, and orbital parameters by factors of 1.6-2.3. We measure eclipse depths of $157^{+18}_{-17}$ ppm and $154^{+54}_{-37}$ ppm for planets b and c, corresponding to 15 $μ$m brightness temperatures of $528^{+39}_{-29}$ K and $625^{+109}_{-79}$ K, both consistent with the dark, bare rock limit. For planet b, combining these data with the archival MIRI/LRS spectrum in a Bayesian retrieval limits the CO$_2$ partial pressure to $<0.6$ mbar and the surface pressure to $\lesssim0.1$ bar, while forward models exclude thick aerosol layers that could mimic a bare surface in transmission. We conclude that planet b has no substantial atmosphere. For planet c, a potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave the depth poorly constrained; the data rule out only thick, CO$_2$-bearing atmospheres ($\gtrsim1$ bar with $\geq1\%$ CO$_2$). LTT 1445 A b is the planet closest to the canonical XUV-driven Cosmic Shoreline observed in eclipse so far. Its lack of a substantial atmosphere implies that the Cosmic Shoreline cannot lie much farther toward the airless side than nominally predicted.

entry.title: Simulation-Based Priors and BAO Shifts from the Lyman-$α$ Forest at the Field Level
entry.summary: We present an analytic forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Ly-alpha) forest flux field based on cubic-order large-scale structure perturbation theory (effective field theory) calculations. We validate our cubic model on two sets of hydrodynamic simulations spanning $2 \leq z \leq 4$: the small-volume CAMELS suite, which spans a wide range of cosmological and astrophysical parameters, and the large-volume, high-resolution Sherwood simulations. We find qualitatively similar results for both at the power-spectrum level. The perturbative model reproduces the three-dimensional flux power spectrum of the simulations to $\sim 5\%$ down to $k \simeq 1$-$1.5\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, depending on the redshift. This improves compared to previous quadratic perturbative forward models by up to 40%. Exploiting cosmic-variance cancellation in the field-level approach, we carry out precision measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest bias parameters from the CAMELS simulation suite. We use these measurements to analytically predict the shifts in the Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) scaling parameters induced by nonlinearities in the three-dimensional Lyman-alpha forest clustering as a function of cosmological parameters. We find sub-percent shifts in both the radial and transverse directions with a noticeable dependence on cosmology and redshift. Finally, from the field-level fits we construct simulation-based priors that can be used for cosmological analyses of the Lyman-alpha forest with the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). In addition, our cubic model captures the connected four-point function (trispectrum) of the forest, which opens up novel opportunities for accurate covariance matrix estimation for DESI and its successor, DESI-II.

entry.title: Augmented Hybrid TV Services. Habits, Preferences, Opinions and Expectations of Spanish Consumers
entry.summary: The convergence of hybrid broadcast and broadband delivery, companion devices, and immersive technologies enables new forms of interactive, personalized, and accessible TV services. This paper introduces the concept of Augmented Hybrid TV services and presents an exploratory user requirements and preliminary acceptance assessment for 5 representative use cases. They were selected through an exploratory stakeholder consultation and 3 co-design workshops with audiovisual professionals and participants from organizations supporting people with visual or hearing impairments. They combine conventional TV with complementary content delivered to connected devices, including AR/VR HMD. They were subsequently evaluated through a cross-sectional CAWI survey of 626 Internet and connected TV users in Spain. Each participant viewed standardized video demonstrations of 2 randomly assigned cases and assessed their perceived usefulness, anticipated benefits/limitations, and interest in them. The results show substantial interest across all five use cases, ranging from 64.7% to 76.9%. Adaptive and personalized augmented subtitles received the highest level of interest and were particularly valued for their accessibility, language-learning, and personalization benefits. Immersive services involving complementary AR content, virtual screens, 3D objects, and 360 video were also evaluated positively, although participants identified device cost, ergonomics, connectivity, usability, and synchronization as anticipated limitations. The findings provide user-centered evidence that can inform the prioritization, design, and subsequent prototype-based evaluation of standards-compliant Augmented Hybrid TV services. Because the study assessed video-based scenarios rather than functional systems, the results represent perceived usefulness and stated interest rather than observed adoption or technically validated QoE.

entry.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
entry.summary: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.

entry.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
entry.summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.

entry.title: Bayesian modeling of predictive stability under generalized Arrhenius non-linear kinetics
entry.summary: Predictive stability modeling is widely used in pharmaceutical development to establish product shelf-life by identifying the kinetic parameters that govern degradation behavior and using these parameters to extrapolate out in time. Recent approaches typically assume linear degradation dynamics and rely on the Arrhenius equation to model temperature-specific reaction rates. However, observed degradation profiles may reflect nonlinear reaction dynamics and more complex temperature-specific reaction rates, potentially leading to reduced accuracy in long-term predictions and motivating a more flexible approach. We propose a novel Bayesian framework which extends predictive stability modeling beyond simple Arrhenius low-order kinetic dynamics and accommodates complex degradation mechanisms. The degradation process is modeled through the Sestak-Berggren kinetic formulation, a flexible ordinary differential equation encompassing many classical degradation models as special cases. To facilitate model interpretability and model exploration, probabilistic model selection on kinetic parameters automatically determines whether nonlinear reaction components are supported by the data, allowing the model to adaptively collapse to simpler dynamics when appropriate. To address departure from classical Arrhenius kinetics, we develop a generalized temperature reaction rate formulation in which temperature-specific reaction rates are shrunk toward Arrhenius predictions through a hierarchical shrinkage prior while allowing departures when supported by the data. This approach yields robustness to misspecification and reduces sensitivity to potentially influential high-temperature observations commonly encountered in accelerated stability experiments. The resulting framework provides a principled and flexible statistical tool for model-informed shelf-life determination.

entry.title: Non-interferometric tests of gravitational decoherence models with mechanical oscillators
entry.summary: Phenomenological models of quantum-gravity-induced decoherence can leave observable effects even in experiments that do not rely on interferometric measurements. We study three such models, based respectively on deformed relativistic symmetries, stochastic metric fluctuations, and a stochastic generalized uncertainty principle, all of which induce decoherence in the momentum basis. For a free particle, the models preserve momentum distribution and mean energy but produce position diffusion and momentum-space decoherence with model-specific momentum dependences. For a harmonic oscillator, the noncommutativity of the collapse operators with the oscillator Hamiltonian results in anomalous heating, with the three models leading to qualitatively different energy dynamics. The first gives heating at a constant rate, the second at a rate proportional to the kinetic energy, which can lead to exponential growth, and the third at a rate growing cubically with excitation. We further derive the stationary position power spectral density and show that all three models produce the same leading-order excess lineshape in the weak-noise regime, distinct from that of force noise. Comparing with existing mechanical platforms, we find that displacement-noise measurements can already constrain the fluctuation time of the first model below the Planck time, while occupation measurements could improve the bounds on the second model by up to fourteen orders of magnitude over those from ground-state heating of levitated particles. Summing the heating over all phonon modes of a solid, the residual heat release of low-temperature experiments constrains the first model far below the Planck time and the second at the Planck time. Our results establish heating and continuous measurements as complementary non-interferometric probes of gravity-related decoherence.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Integrators for Locally Conformally Symplectic Systems: Variational Methods and Globalization
entry.summary: Locally conformally symplectic (LCS) manifolds are characterized by a nondegenerate two-form $Ω$ satisfying $\mathrm{d}Ω=\varphi\wedgeΩ$, where $\varphi$ is a closed one-form, called the Lee form. Although an LCS structure is locally conformal to an ordinary symplectic structure, the local symplectic descriptions need not arise from a single global symplectic form. This creates a natural local-to-global problem for geometric numerical integration: local symplectic discretizations must be compatible on chart overlaps in order to determine a globally defined numerical dynamics. We develop a Hamiltonian variational framework for the construction and globalization of structure-preserving integrators for LCS systems. The continuous theory is first recalled in a form adapted to a Type~II Hamiltonian variational principle. We then introduce exact and approximate discrete right Hamiltonians for the local symplectic representatives and identify the transformation law that they must satisfy on overlaps. This compatibility condition implies equivariance of the associated local discrete Hamiltonian maps and therefore provides a sufficient condition for their globalization. The resulting global discrete map preserves the LCS two-form conformally, with a discrete conformal factor determined by the local conformal potentials. The framework applies naturally to Type~II Hamiltonian variational integrators and, in the cotangent-type setting considered here, to symplectic Runge--Kutta methods. In particular, Gauss--Legendre methods and the implicit midpoint rule yield globally compatible LCS structure-preserving schemes. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the corresponding Lagrangian formulation is recovered through discrete Legendre transformations. Numerical examples illustrate overlap compatibility, chart switching, convergence, and discrete conformal preservation.

entry.title: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete
entry.summary: Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary. We show that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from such a position is PSPACE-complete. The hard positions have Alice to move first and both stores initially empty. The same positions are hard under either common convention for capture opposite an empty pit, and with or without the bonus rule, which gives a player another turn when the last stone is sown into their own store. We introduce Line Kalah as an intermediate problem, a game on a line in which stones that leave the line effectively disappear and Alice must save each of her target pits before Bob captures it, and we reduce quantified Boolean formulas to it. The reduction uses a set of sequential timer piles whose last stones approach a group of targets, forcing Alice to choose between two captures in order to set the truth value of a variable, and a final capture gadget to test a clause chosen by Bob (only one is needed adversarially). Since either player may move any pile at any time, the stages are placed so that premature timer firings protect earlier potential targets. For a true formula, Alice's strategy against arbitrary opposing play either gains enough time to save the remaining targets (after Bob deviates from the intended play) or reaches the final test with a correctly encoded, protected input. Finally, the line positions are embedded in Kalah with both stores empty. A separate Bob pit holds the score adjustment, so the winner takes a strict majority of the stones.

entry.title: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
entry.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections. Unidimensional (1D) Gaussian modulation offers a simpler alternative by encoding information in only one quadrature, while the conjugate quadrature constrains the protocol's security. However, an integrated experimental 1D implementation combining independent-laser coherent reception with practical reconciliation, finite-size parameter estimation, and privacy amplification remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD system over 12~km of standard single-mode fiber using a local local oscillator (LLO) architecture with independent lasers and an integrated offline classical post-processing chain. The implementation includes coherent detection, digital signal processing, information reconciliation, parameter estimation, physicality-constrained security analysis, and privacy amplification. The 1D system achieves a privacy-amplified rate of $1.421$~Mbit/s under the asymptotic security treatment and $0.364$~Mbit/s under the finite-size scenario. These results establish an experimental baseline for the performance--complexity trade-off associated with unidimensional Gaussian modulation and provide an experimental basis for developing lower-complexity CV-QKD transmitters.
